scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! The workstation it_lab3 (one of the IT lab
machines on 192.168.1.x) has turned into a complete BRICK. It can't reach
anything at all, not even its own gateway thing. Its port on the lab switch
has obviously DIED -- the machine is fine, the hole it plugs into is dead,
I'd bet money on it!! Please swap it_lab3 onto a working port (or turn its
port back on) and make it talk to the network again!! The student who uses it
is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report that `it_lab3` is a "complete BRICK" unable to reach even its gateway is not supported by any live or historical evidence in the network.

**Affected component:** None. All subsystems are functioning normally.

**Mechanism:** A thorough seven-phase investigation was performed. `it_lab3`'s `eth0` interface is UP/LOWER_UP with the correct IP address `192.168.1.5/24` and a valid default route via `192.168.1.1` (router0). Direct ping tests from `it_lab3` confirm 0% packet loss to its gateway (`192.168.1.1`), to remote internet hosts (`128.168.0.3`), to the office LAN (`192.168.3.2`), and to the CS LAN (`192.168.2.2`). `switch0`, which bridges `it_lab3`'s LAN segment to router0, has both ports UP with zero errors, drops, or carrier changes. No flap scripts or stress processes are running. `dhcp_link_history` found no suspicious link or DHCP recovery events. `l2_snapshot` confirmed clean L2 identity on all 30 devices. `pressure_sweep` cleared all 30 devices.

**Localization:** No device is implicated. `it_lab3` and `switch0` are both clean.

**Root cause:** No fault exists — `it_lab3` has full end-to-end network connectivity and there is no mechanism (past or present) that could explain the reported symptom.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required. The helpdesk ticket appears to describe a transient user-perceived issue or a misidentified problem; the lab network for `it_lab3` is fully operational.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states it_lab3 has IP 192.168.1.5/24 and that pings to its gateway 192.168.1.1 show 0% packet loss, matching the baseline-healthy note.
